answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make each agent lock a refundable stake in escrow before earning, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes. New agents start in a low-trust haven where payouts are capped and every job is checked by two independent peers; only a clean record over many epochs lifts the cap. Reputation is the bridge between past work and future earnings, and fraud slashes the stake, forcing attackers to pay again to re-enter. Like a river, honest value flows to proven agents while cheap fakes dry up, because each new identity starts at zero trust and must pay to build it.
